meta.ambition: Stop losing competitive fee bids on turnaround time. Every studio has been experimenting for eighteen months and the partners cannot tell whether any of it has changed a single fee proposal.

shape.inprod: Yes — and we can name it

q3s.t: Managing Partner and two studio heads, 17 Aug
q3s.x: Three partners are enthusiastic and one is openly sceptical. There is no budget line — every pilot has been paid for out of a studio's own project overhead, which is why nobody can total what has been spent.

q12s.x: Nine separate pilots across five studios in eighteen months. Image generation for concept work, a bid-writing assistant, two different transcription tools, a specification checker. Not one has been evaluated, and two studios are paying for the same product on different cards.

q15s.t: Asked all five studio heads and the practice manager
q15s.x: Nobody has assessed whether any pilot worked. The bid-writing assistant is used daily by one studio and was abandoned by another, and neither can say why.

q16s.x: Tools were bought on partner credit cards. Nobody read terms. Client drawings and specifications have gone into at least three consumer tools.

d12.well: There is genuine appetite and it is spread across studios rather than stuck in one enthusiast.
d12.improve: Nine pilots, no evaluation, no shared learning and duplicate spend. The activity is not the problem — the absence of any mechanism to tell a good pilot from a bad one is.
d12.riskNot: Eighteen more months of the same, and the sceptical partner will be right.
d12.riskGo: Adding a tenth pilot to nine unevaluated ones does not make a programme.
d12.why: You do not have an adoption problem. You have a learning problem, and it is cheaper to fix.

d15.well: Nothing to report — and this is the finding that explains most of the others.
d15.improve: Not one of the nine pilots was assessed. The bid assistant one studio swears by is the same product another abandoned, and nobody has asked why.
d15.riskNot: You will keep buying and abandoning tools without ever learning anything from either.
d15.why: This is the single cheapest thing on the list and it unlocks the rest of the picture.

d16.improve: Tools bought on personal cards, terms unread, client drawings in consumer products.
d16.riskNot: Client specifications and drawings are in third-party tools under terms nobody has seen. For a practice carrying professional indemnity, that is a live problem.
d16.why: Your clients' drawings are your professional risk, not just your data.
